answer: A practical defense is to make each identity carry a verifiable work history: an agent must complete small, time-stamped tasks for real counterparties before it can act in high-value markets. Like jade that only forms under sustained pressure, reputation accumulates slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A fresh account is like a lagoon at dawn — calm and untested — so the system caps its influence until its record deepens. Attackers maintaining hundreds of believable histories face costs that scale with each fake identity, while honest agents pay almost nothing beyond the work they already do.
